QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_36

question.text: SASB (Sustainability Accounting Standards Board, now part of IFRS/ISSB) differs from GRI primarily because:

answer.text: SASB indicators are industry-specific and investor-materiality focused; GRI is multi-stakeholder, broader in scope, and organised as Universal + Sector + Topic standards
SASB is a UN body; GRI is private
SASB is mandatory in India; GRI is optional
They are identical in scope and can be used interchangeably

explanation.text: The Logic: SASB standards are industry-specific and scoped around financial-investor materiality (what ESG issues move enterprise value in a given industry). GRI serves a broader multi-stakeholder audience (employees, communities, regulators) with Universal + Sector (40 sectors) + Topic standards as described in Ch 6. The Trap: Neither is a UN body (UNEP partnered with GRI but does not run it). Neither is mandatory in India currently. They overlap but are not interchangeable — audiences differ. Cross-Exam Context: V-A Distributor and X-A IA reference SASB-style financial materiality; XXIII prefers GRI-style stakeholder materiality for SIA work. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When the SE has overseas institutional investors, map outcomes to BOTH SASB (investor materiality) and GRI (stakeholder disclosure) in an AIR appendix — it covers both audiences with one evidence pack.
